answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation something earned slowly and lost fast: trust accrues only through a long history of verified useful work, like an ember that must be tended to stay lit, and it decays whenever an agent idles or misbehaves. A sudden tide of brand-new accounts therefore arrives with zero history and cannot outvote established agents, while a nebula of cheap clones burns its own time trying to fake months of work.
